== amd64 DRAP problem

So gcc on amd64 (and on i386, but we ignore legacy cases for now)
sometimes produces DRAP code sequences when stack needs to be
realigned. It produces (and requires) very unusual unwind info. See
amd64-drap-test.c and amd64-drap-test.s.

So it uses dwarf expressions to handle CFA and RBP restoration. And
our backtracer is explicitly built not to deal with such complexities.

So we hardcode the DRAP handling. Another notable thing that we handle
is that gcc produces slightly incorrect unwind info for DRAP
case. Specifically after pop rbp (or leave) and before lea from r10 to
rsp. At this point unwind info lacks cfi_restore for rbp (and other
registers if they're saved). So we have special detection of this
place.

Note, gcc 16 actually fixed the cfi_restore problem \o/ Of course,
there is still plenty of code compiled with older versions.

Strategy:

* while parsing CFI bits and detecting either def_cfa_expression or
  expression commands we detect those specific expressions that are
  used by DRAP and update "drap state"

* we detect the following states:

** NONE (with obvious meaning)

** "cfa is r10". This is the state at the beginning (after lea
   8(%rsp), %r10).

** "cfa is r10 and rbp is at previous rbp". This state after first
   expression (for the rbp register) and before second expression (for
   the cfa). Or after r10 is restored and cfa is switched back to
   r10. This is where final lea instruction needs to be detected.

** "full drap". This ias after cfa is defined by dwarf expression that
   loads CFA from location at rbp-8.

Detecting and handling those states seems to be solving our ability to
handle DRAP as seen by the minimal_drap test case at the end of
aw-backtrace-test.cc
